title: Navigating the Digital Support Gap: A Qualitative Exploration of Digital Health Information Practices and Unmet Needs Among Long-term Cancer Survivors
summary: After cancer treatment, many people increasingly need to find and assess health information on their own. Websites, search engines, social media, apps, and other digital services can play an important role. This study explores how adults after cancer search for, understand, assess, and use health information in everyday life, what support they feel is missing, and which digital services they experience as helpful or problematic. Participants take part in one individual interview lasting approximately 45 to 60 minutes. The interviews are then systematically analysed. The findings are intended to improve understanding of information and support needs in life after cancer and to inform further research.

interventions.name: Adult long-term cancer survivors participate in one semi-structured qualitative individual interview lasting approximately 45–60 minutes. Interviews may be conducted in person, by telephone, or via an institutionally approved videoconferencing system. Interviews are audio-recorded following written

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
History of cancer and completion of at least one acute phase of primary oncological treatment. Sufficient German-language proficiency to understand the study information and informed consent and to participate in an approximately 45–60-minute interview in German. Current ability to provide informed consent and to participate meaningfully in the interview. Written consent to participation, including audio recording, transcription, and pseudonymised scientific analysis. Ongoing follow-up care and maintenance, endocrine, immunological, targeted, or other long-term treatments do not exclude participation provided that there is currently no intensive acute treatment context. Recurrence or progression alone is not an exclusion criterion.
Exclusion criteria:
Current intensive acute oncological treatment because of newly diagnosed, recurrent, or progressive cancer, regardless of treatment modality. Current specialised palliative or hospice care if it substantially overrides the post-acute survivorship context; palliative treatment intent or advanced disease alone does not constitute an exclusion criterion. Current inability to provide informed consent or to participate meaningfully in the interview, for example because of acute psychological, cognitive, or comparable impairment. Insufficient German-language proficiency for study information, informed consent, and interview participation. No consent to audio recording.
